title: OPERA: Achieving Secure and High-performance OLAP with Parallelized Homomorphic Comparisons
abstract: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is increasingly adopted in Online Analytical Processing (OLAP) systems to protect against data breaches. However, existing FHE-based OLAP systems must sequentially execute computationally intensive homomorphic comparisons for query processing on FHE ciphertexts, leading to significantly lower performance compared to traditional OLAP systems. We present OPERA, the first high-performance FHE-based OLAP system on the GPU. Observing the redundancy in reexecuting homomorphic comparisons from scratch, we design HOMCACHE to create a GPU-accelerated parallel query execution workflow: OPERA selectively caches comparison results and allows subsequent comparisons to reuse them, thereby reducing the computational cost per comparison and facilitating concurrent execution of multiple comparisons on the GPU. Nevertheless, due to the large size of FHE ciphertexts, HOMCACHE can grow substantially, and naively applying traditional plaintext-oriented cache management strategies like LRU results in suboptimal performance. To ensure stable high performance, we develop a density-driven algorithm tailored for managing ciphertexts in HOMCACHE. Compared to notable baselines running on CPUs, OPERA reduces query latency by up to 9612x with 1.2GB cache storage without compromising security. OPERA's source code, complete benchmark suite, and raw results are available at github.com/hku-systems/Opera.

Introduction With the rapid advancement of cloud computing, many entities (e.g., enterprises and government institutions) are increasingly moving private data to the cloud for Online Analytical Processing (OLAP) tasks, such as medical diag- nosis [ 1] and financial analysis [ 2]. However, the frequent data breaches, causing average losses of $9.48 million per incident [ 3], reveal that existing security mechanisms in OLAP systems (e.g., access control [ 4], disk encryption [ 5]) are ineffective at protecting sensitive data on public clouds. O PERA paral- lelizes such workflow, particularly the homomorphic comparisons, and is adapted to run on a GPU to enhance performance further. systems, as it enables unlimited additions and multiplica- tions on ciphertexts while providing strong standard security guarantees [ 6]. Since OLAP queries, such as those in TPC- H[ 7], typically involve several filtering predicates (e.g., ≤) and aggregation operators (e.g., SUM), an FHE-based secure OLAP system must support homomorphic filtering and aggregation to process queries on FHE ciphertexts. Prior systems (e.g., HE 3DB [ 8] and HEDA [ 9]) employ a sequential filter-aggregation workflow to support secure OLAP . As shown in Figure 1, these systems process queries by linearly scanning database records and performing mul- tiple homomorphic comparisons between each record and the filtering predicate. Each comparison generates a filter; multiple filters are aggregated. Then, the aggregated fil- ter is applied to exclude irrelevant records, the remaining records are aggregated as final query results. However, their performance is significantly lower than traditional OLAP systems [10]. For instance, when running HE 3DB on TPC-H Q6 with 128 records of 16-bit and 26-bit sizes, we observed high query latencies of 143s and 217s, respectively (§ 6). We attribute this low performance to the sequential workflow, where all homomorphic comparisons are executed sequentially. Prior work focuses on parallelizing FHE operations ( Layer 0 ), homomorphic comparisons remain sequential ( Layer 2 ) during OLAP . process on this difference to extract the Most Significant Bit (MSB), with each iteration running two or more costly FHE operations (e.g., bootstrapping [ 11]). In a prior OLAP sys- tem with N records and a query with M filtering predicates, N∗M comparisons need to be executed sequentially without overlap. Our theoretical and empirical analysis (§ 2.3) shows that these sequential comparisons can consume over 90% of the query execution time in typical OLAP workloads. A viable solution for improving query efficiency is parallelizing homomorphic comparisons on hardware accel- erators, such as GPUs. Although previous work [ 12] has explored parallelizing FHE operations like bootstrapping on accelerators, this approach yields limited performance gains in OLAP systems, as multiple comparisons are still sequen- tially executed and remain non-parallelizable. As shown in Figure 2, the key reason is that even with operation paral- lelization within a single iteration ( Layer 0 ), the substantial computational demands across multiple iterations for a sin- gle comparison ( Layer 1) still exceed GPU capacity, leaving limited resources for comparison parallelism in Layer 2 . We observe that the main obstacle to improving query performance lies in the multiple non-parallelizable iterations required by homomorphic comparisons, our key idea is to cache a subset of comparison results (i.e., filters) and allow subsequent comparisons to compute over selected cached filters for reducing the iterations needed. For each compar- ison, we select cached filters whose filtering predicates are numerically closest to the current comparison's predicates. This minimizes the numerical difference (i.e., bit-width [ 8]) between the predicates of compared ciphertexts, allowing the difference to be stored with fewer bits thus reducing the iterations needed to extract the MSB. As fewer iterations lower the resource demands per comparison without ex- ceeding GPU capacity, this facilitates concurrently executing multiple comparisons on the GPU. This paper presents O PERA 1, the first high-performance FHE-based OLAP system featuring parallelized homomor- phic comparisons on the GPU. We introduce H OM CACHE to create a new parallel query execution workflow, as shown in Figure 1.H OM CACHE meticulously manages the insertion and eviction of generated filters for OLAP queries. During filter generation, O PERA minimizes the cost of comparisons by reducing iterations through the reuse of cached filters from H OM CACHE , and by parallelizing FHE operations to accelerate each iteration. By lowering the cost of each com- 1. O PERA means OLAP with ParallElized homomoRphic compArisons. parison, multiple comparisons can be executed in parallel on the GPU. For aggregation, similar to the prior workflow, OPERA applies the generated filter to all records to exclude irrelevant and aggregate the remaining records. However, even with the parallel workflow, O PERA still faces two major challenges. The first challenge is to ef- ficiently managing H OM CACHE , as its size grows almost linearly due to the homomorphically encrypted cached fil- ters. Since comparisons are expected to be performed on cached filters with numerically close filtering predicates, traditional eviction strategies (e.g., LRU [ 13]) are ineffective in this setting and may lead to the unexpected eviction of optimal filters because they do not consider the critical metric of numerical distance among cached objects (filters), which is essential for efficiently parallelizing homomorphic comparisons. To tackle this performance challenge, we formalize it as a convex optimization problem and propose a density-driven eviction algorithm. This algorithm evaluates the density of filters, which relates to their numerical distances, to estimate the potential benefit of a newly generated filter. It compares this benefit with existing cached filters and evicts the one with the lowest benefit. This ensures a stable reduction in computational cost for comparisons, enabling high paral- lelism in O PERA 's workflow. The second challenge is ensuring correct comparisons. Although O PERA reduces the number of bits needed to store the difference between compared FHE ciphertexts, overflow may occur if the difference is too large. For instance, if a query with a filtering parameter of 220 is compared to a record with a value of 22, the resulting difference (i.e., FHE(220-22)) may exceed the reduced storage capacity, causing overflow and leading to an inaccurate comparison. To tackle this correctness challenge, O PERA shepherds homomorphic comparisons using a unique zone-based hi- erarchical correction algorithm. For each comparison, the algorithm divides the entire comparison space, i.e., the range of differences, into multiple zones and hierarchi- cally corrects the results within each zone using dedicated cached filters. This algorithm is efficient, requiring only lightweight operations (e.g., AND and OR) for correction, ensuring O PERA 's workflow runs at high performance. We implemented O PERA on the HE 3DB codebase [ 8], replacing the original CPU SEAL library [ 14] with GPU Phantom library [ 15], and creates a CUDA version of TFHEpp [ 16] to enable GPU-accelerated comparison par- allelization. We compared O PERA with notable FHE-based OLAP systems using the standard TPC-H benchmark [ 7]. The evaluation shows that: • OPERA is efficient. O PERA achieved a 1064x speedup in homomorphic comparisons with our parallel query execution workflow, resulting in up to 9612x lower query latency compared to baseline systems across diverse fil- tering predicates and aggregation operators, using 1.2GB storage of H OM CACHE (§6.1,§ 6.2). • OPERA is stable.
